payload.prompt: We have a new employee named Charles Taylor, born 21. October 1994. Please create them as an employee with email charles.taylor@example.org and start date 3. June 2026.

payload.goal: Create a new employee record for Charles Taylor with the provided personal details, email, and start date.
success_checks: Employee 'Charles Taylor' exists in the system
Date of birth is set to 1994-10-21
Employment start date is set to 2026-06-03
risk_notes: No phone number provided; may be required depending on system configuration
No department or position/title specified; may need to be assigned later
No salary or payroll details provided; payroll setup will be incomplete until added
No address information provided; may be required for tax/payroll compliance
payload.suggested_first_action: POST /employee with firstName='Charles', lastName='Taylor', dateOfBirth='1994-10-21', email='charles.taylor@example.org', startDate='2026-06-03'
ordered_steps: POST /employee { firstName: 'Charles', lastName: 'Taylor', dateOfBirth: '1994-10-21', email: 'charles.taylor@example.org', startDate: '2026-06-03' }
Verify response returns a valid employee ID
Confirm employee record is retrievable via GET /employee/{id}
Optionally assign department, position, and payroll details via PUT /employee/{id}

planned_endpoints.summary: Find employees corresponding with sent data.

rules: ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'NO_ACCESS' (safest default — avoids 422 errors). Only use 'STANDARD' if email login is explicitly needed.
startDate is a TOP-LEVEL field on the employee object. Do NOT put it inside an employments array.
dateOfBirth is a TOP-LEVEL field. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
jobTitle is set via PUT /employee/{id} AFTER creation — it cannot be set in the initial POST.
Do NOT include an 'employments' array in POST /employee — employment details go via separate POST /employee/employment endpoint.

For occupation codes (STYRK/yrkeskode): POST /employee/employment first, then GET /employee/employment/occupationCode?nameAndCode=XXXX to find the code, then PUT /employee/employment/details to set it.
For update tasks, GET /employee with fields=* first so you have id and version.
PUT /employee/{id} MUST include id and version from the GET response.
Only send the fields the prompt explicitly asks to change.
If the prompt asks for admin/access privileges, use grant_employee_entitlements instead of guessing employee fields.
